tasks.title: Wire one regional OCR adapter so production can boot at all

steps: Pick azure-di (shortest path: @azure-rest/ai-document-intelligence, prebuilt-read model).
Implement extract() in azure-document-intelligence.provider.ts against this.cfg.endpoint/apiKey in this.cfg.region.
Map the response to OcrExtractionResult (rawText + per-field confidences) exactly as openai-ocr.provider.ts does.
Flip capabilities.implemented to true ONLY once extract() is real — the flag is what the boot guard reads.
Fix test/residency.spec.ts fixture: it hardcodes implemented:true on a provider it calls "azure-di", which is why the suite never caught this.
Re-run apps/api/test/ocr-deadlock.spec.ts — the azure-di case must now fail, and that is the signal to update it.
tasks.credentials_required: Azure Document Intelligence endpoint + key in the target region
tasks.security_considerations: Regional endpoint only — the whole point of the guard is that raw identity documents never leave the residency region.
tasks.completion_evidence: azure-di implemented (REST via fetch, no new dependency); 15 provider tests + 5 invariant tests; ocr-capability and residency fixtures corrected. NOT yet run against a live Azure endpoint — that still needs a key.

tasks.reason: The API origin port answers on the public internet without TLS, bypassing nginx.

tasks.title: Implement the data-retention policy (documents and PII have no TTL)
tasks.reason: COMPLIANCE.md §7 documents a retention policy as a proposal; nothing enforces it. Identity documents are kept indefinitely.
tasks.evidence: VISAAIDocs security/COMPLIANCE.md:158 "Retention policy — proposal [gap: not implemented]"; SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md row 5 marks it P1.
steps: Define a per-data-class TTL (documents, OCR text, voice recordings, audit events).
Add a scheduled worker that deletes or anonymises past TTL.
Record each deletion in the privacy audit trail (the same path PRIV-002 fixed).
Reconcile the privacy policy text with what the worker actually does.
tasks.security_considerations: Deletion must be irreversible and audited; a soft-delete is not retention.

tasks.title: Ratchet the 1,868 lint errors down instead of suppressing them
tasks.reason: Lint carries no signal at 1,868 errors — a genuine new error is invisible. That is how a broken money-path e2e went unnoticed.
tasks.evidence: apps/api eslint: 1,868 errors / 562 warnings across 301 files, overwhelmingly @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-* where `any` escapes Supabase and Stripe clients.
steps: Commit the current error count as a baseline.
Add a CI step that fails when the count RISES — no new unsafe code, without a big-bang fix.
Type the Supabase boundary first (generated DB types already exist); it is the largest cluster and the one where a schema change becomes a silent runtime error.
Do NOT bulk-add eslint-disable — that destroys the signal rather than the debt.
Note the `lint` script runs eslint with --fix, so invoking it rewrites files; the ratchet step must use a non-fixing invocation.
tasks.security_considerations: no-unsafe-* on database results is not style — it is where an unvalidated shape reaches business logic.
tasks.completion_evidence: Ratchet built, self-tested both directions and wired into CI. Errors 1,865 -> 1,034 (-45%) by scoping no-unsafe-* to production code (71% of the count was in specs/fixtures, where a test double is an `any` on purpose). Baseline committed at apps/api/.lint-baseline.json.

tasks.title: Bind the generated Supabase types and clear the 59 errors they surface
tasks.reason: The database boundary is the least type-safe part of the app. A column that becomes nullable in a migration currently produces no compile error anywhere.
tasks.evidence: Types generated and committed (packages/types/src/database.types.ts, 140 tables). Flipping `Db = SupabaseClient<Database>` was MEASURED: 59 errors across 19 files. iam 16, provenance 13, verification 6, audit 4, then 1-2 each. They are real: provenance assigns `string | null` to `string`; kpi-rollup passes a `text` column where a `SubPlan` union is required.
steps: Flip `Db` to `SupabaseClient<Database>` in supabase.service.ts.
Work file by file in the recorded order (iam is already done as the worked example).
Use CHECKED boundary mappers like iam.repository.impl.ts toRole/toOrganization — NOT `as` casts. A cast launders exactly the defect the change surfaces.
For each nullable-vs-non-null mismatch decide deliberately: widen the domain type, or handle the null at the boundary. Do not default it silently.
Regenerate types after every migration; add that to the migration checklist.
tasks.security_considerations: Each narrowing must be validated, not asserted. An unrecognised role key flowing through the permission system typed as valid is the failure mode.
